silence noun

also in silence, keep silent, break the silence, stillness, silence, please!, quiet, please!

classical

Liv. 1.13.4: silentium et repentīna fit quiēs
Cic. de Or. 3.143 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 31, 379

silentium, silentiī n.

noun, second declension

silence, stillness

Of people and of places. silentiō or per silentium, “in silence”; silentium facere, “to call for silence” (see quiet!); silentium tenēre (Livy), “to keep silent”; silentia rumpere, “to break the silence”, is poetic.

Other words

  • taciturnitās, taciturnitātis f. — keeping silent, holding one’s tongue

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Publ. Syr. T 16

    A person’s silence, not speaking or not telling; silentium is the stillness itself.

  • tacitē — in silence, without a word

    adverb · also used · classical · Aug. Conf. 6.3.3: legentem vīdimus tacitē; Phaedr. 1.2.17: tacitē prōfert ē stagnō caput

    Also secretly, unnoticed. The adjective tacitus goes with the person: Tacitus citius audiēs (Ter. Eun. 571).

Examples

  • silentium et repentīna fit quiēs

    there is silence, and a sudden calmLiv. 1.13.4

  • nōndum cristātī rūpēre silentia gallī

    the crested cocks have not yet broken the silenceMart. 9.68.3

  • arripuī, aperuī, et lēgī in silentiō

    I snatched it up, opened it and read in silenceAug. Conf. 8.12.29

  • Silentium, quaesō!

    Silence, please!Traupman 25

See also quiet!, be quiet, noise, peace, in a low voice.
